title: Backport Report Schema
description: Schema for *-backport-report.json reports produced by the backport-fix skill. Records the outcome of propagating a security fix to multiple release branches via the Amalgamator pipeline. Every string below is untrusted when it reaches a consumer: repositories are clone targets, refs are checkout targets, paths are open targets, so each is constrained to what the consumer can safely act on. The artifact declares what happened; it never declares a command to run.

target_branches.description: Per-branch backport results. One entry per target release branch, and exactly one entry per branch.

notes.description: Free-form notes — caveats, manual steps needed, anything a reviewer should know.

git_ref.description: A branch or ref name. Same charset as remediation.schema.json $defs/fork.fix_branch, minus a leading '-': the value is handed to git checkout/fetch, where a leading dash is read as an option.

relative_path.description: A workspace-relative path. Not absolute and never containing '..': consumers open these, and a path from an artifact must not escape the workspace it is resolved in.

repo_url.description: A clone URL. Only https and ssh are accepted: consumers hand this to git clone, where the ext:: transport executes arbitrary commands and file: (or a bare path) reads outside the workspace.

full_commit_sha.description: A full 40-hex commit SHA. Abbreviated SHAs are not identities: verification.schema.json requires the same of the patched_commit this value is passed as.

check.description: A build or test invocation recorded as evidence. `command` is a historical record of what ran, never an instruction for a consumer to execute.

command.description: The command that was run, recorded for audit. Never executed by a consumer.

repository.description: Upstream repository URL the fix was applied to.

logical_product.description: Logical product this repo belongs to.

additional.description: Producer-declared run records the contract does not declare yet (run_id, model, registry_sha, ...). Open on purpose: a closed metadata object turns every new producer field into a breaking contract change.

commit.description: SHA of the fix commit being backported. A reference, so abbreviations are accepted here; the backport side requires the full SHA.

branch.description: Branch the fix was originally applied to.

fork_url.description: URL of the private fork where the fix lives.

remediation_path.description: Path to the *-remediation.json that produced the fix.

finding_refs.description: Finding references from the source remediation.

branch_result.description: One target branch. A success carries evidence of what landed; a failure names why the run stopped.

stop_reason.description: Why the run did not produce a backport on this branch. Required when status is failed.

checks.description: Build and test runs for this branch, each with its outcome. A run that was never attempted is absent, which is a different claim from a skipped one.

cost_usd.description: LLM API cost for this branch's backport run.

patch_files_changed.description: Number of files changed in the candidate patch.

backport_commit.description: SHA of the backport commit on the target branch (from Amalgamator's preserved branch). Passed to verify-remediation as the patched_commit.

backport_branch.description: Branch where Amalgamator committed the backport (e.g. 'amalgamator/backport-crio-stats-nil-panic-release-1-33'). Can be passed to verify-remediation as the patched ref.

error.description: Error message if the backport failed.

verification_hint.description: Pre-filled inputs for verify-remediation, so downstream automation can trigger verification without assembling them by hand. Present when at least one branch succeeded. It declares inputs only and deliberately carries no example command line: a string from an artifact is never executed by a consumer.

original_audit_report.description: Path to the *-security-audit.json the findings came from.

repository.description: Repository URL to clone for verification.

branches.description: Per-branch verification targets — only branches whose status is succeeded.

backport_commit.description: Commit SHA to check out for verification.

backport_branch.description: Named branch to check out for verification.

summary.description: Counts DERIVED from target_branches. JSON Schema cannot express the arithmetic, so BackportReport (models/backport.py) enforces total == len(target_branches) and succeeded + failed + skipped == total, and readers recompute rather than trust these numbers.
summary.$comment: total == len(target_branches); succeeded + failed + skipped == total; succeeded counts status == succeeded.

total.description: Total number of target branches attempted.
